question: A facilities project still has last year's contractor safety standard uploaded as project knowledge, and Claude keeps quoting its old inspection interval with complete confidence. Which two actions actually resolve this? Select two.
options: A) Move the project onto a more capable model tier, which will state the inspection interval more accurately.
B) Replace the uploaded file with the current standard so the outdated interval cannot be retrieved again.
C) Add an instruction telling Claude to take particular care whenever any inspection interval is mentioned.
D) Open a fresh conversation and put the same question to Claude once again, this time much more firmly worded.
E) Re-check the inspection dates already issued on the strength of answers quoting the superseded figure.
correct_answers: B) Replace the uploaded file with the current standard so the outdated interval cannot be retrieved again.
E) Re-check the inspection dates already issued on the strength of answers quoting the superseded figure.
explanations: A stronger model reads the same outdated file and repeats the same wrong interval just as confidently.
Correct. The knowledge source is wrong, not the model, so nothing improves until the superseded document is replaced.
An instruction to be careful cannot compensate for a source that is authoritative-looking and out of date.
Rewording or insisting changes nothing when the retrieved document itself contains the wrong number.
Correct for a separate reason: fixing the source does not undo the decisions already taken on bad information, which still need remediation.
